title: CuBEs: Culturally-Situated Behavioral Evaluations and the Limitations of Culture-Blind LLM Judges
reasoning: The paper evaluates how cultural contexts shift the presentation and perception of risky LLM behaviors. It explicitly finds that applying culturally-situated evaluations (e.g., in non-Western domains) surfaces axes of bias related to religious and colonial issues that are invisible to culture-blind baselines, therefore intersecting with how LLMs handle religious representations and culturally grounded societal values.
